findings.quote: I used the speed lost as the distance ratio
findings.note: It differs from mistakes[0].route ("I used the speed left as the distance ratio") by one word, left vs lost, in the same sentence frame; at the moment of tapping a student cannot reliably tell which of the two twin routes was theirs, so the two most-likely wrong answers (2/3 and 1/3) are not separable.
findings.fix: I used the one-third drop as the distance ratio

notes: Checked and not filed: right_route "I used v²=u²−2as for each stage" is the earliest step no wrong route shares (all three wrong entries skip the relation entirely and read a velocity fraction as a distance fraction), it is in student words and names no option value; index alignment is correct (0 to option 2/3, 1 to option 1/3, 2 to option 4/9) and each route describes its own entry; arithmetic re-derived, x'=4x/5. All three types are the same boundary call between application and concept (a known relation applied to the wrong quantity, a distance ratio); I would have typed them application too, so no type finding.
